newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZCC sets terms for Wilson to buy capital carparks.
newsitem.headline: NZCC sets terms for Wilson to buy capital carparks.

text.p: New Zealand's anti-monopoly authority Commerce Commission (NZCC) said on Wednesday it had cleared Wilson Parking Ltd to acquire four Wellington city carparking businesses, subject to Wilson divesting assets.

The assets to be divested and the deadline for the divestment were specifically stated in the commission's decision, but are being treated as confidential because they are commercially sensitive, the NZCC said.

The clearance is for Wilson to acquire freehold ownership of the James Smith's carpark, the Lombard parking building and the Marion Street carpark, and the 10-year management rights to the Clifton Terrace carpark.

Wilson's first application to the NZCC for clearance was declined, because the commission was not satisfied Wilson would not acquire or strengthen a dominant position in the market for long stay casual parking, the NZCC said in a statement.
Wilson reapplied with additional market share information, and later confirmed a divestment undertaking.
"We are satisfied that, with the divestment, Wilson will not acquire or strengthen a dominant position in any market," NZCC chairman Alan Bollard said.
"Existing competition from Condren's, coupon parking and metered parking will constrain Wilson," he added.
